commits.message: stop the ai/edge deploy build OOMing (concurrency + reliable cache)
commits.body:
The build-images ai/edge jobs failed/hung repeatedly on v0.1.45: the Dockerfile
default TURBO_BUILD_CONCURRENCY=10 builds @engenty/ai + all 28 modules with
tsup --dts (1-2 GB per worker) and OOMs the runner — @engenty/projects#build
died with ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY. CI already caps this at 4 on the same
runner class; the image build never got the override (DEPLOY.md documents 4 for
constrained hosts). Pin TURBO_BUILD_CONCURRENCY=4 via build-arg.

Also harden the build step:
- registry-backed layer cache (GHCR) instead of type=gha — the 10 GB GHA cache
  cap + export stalls were behind the earlier build-push hang; no cap on GHCR.
- 45-min per-step timeout so a genuine stall fails ~15min before the job cap
  instead of hanging the full hour.

Remote turbo cache wiring (TURBO_API/TURBO_TOKEN into the Docker build) lands
with the cache server.

commits.message:
feat(modules): load registry-installed modules from node_modules (Level A / A3)

Compose the app from modules installed via the registry (node_modules), not
just workspace modules/ — the 'install a module' half of Level A.

New plugin source "registry" in engenty.plugins: resolveEnabledModules (both
the runtime @engenty/environment twin and the build-script twin) resolves such
a module's dir to node_modules/<packageName> (default @engenty/<slug>,
overridable via .package for names like @engenty/pdf-templates-module).
Everything else funnels through that single seam:

- UI catalog + Tailwind (plugin-artifact-generator): the convention resolvers
  now accept node_modules roots, so a registry module is cataloged (imported
  via its package export) and its ui/ source is registered as a Tailwind
  @source — the source ships in the tarball (A1), which is what makes the
  Tailwind scan work.
- Migrations (aggregate-module-migrations): registry modules contribute
  owners from node_modules; the workspace scan now excludes registry slugs so
  a lingering modules/<slug> checkout can't duplicate them.
- Runtime discovery (core loader): registry modules are appended as package
  candidates and load exactly like workspace modules (server + AI face are
  jiti-loaded from the package source). A registry module shadows any leftover
  workspace candidate of the same slug.

Verified end-to-end against a packed tasks tarball extracted into node_modules:
catalog + Tailwind @source point at node_modules, migrations aggregate, config
check passes, environment/core/ui suites green (+4 new registry-resolution
tests). Browser-level Tailwind confirmation (a real UI build) is the one
follow-up. publishConfig/registry wiring is A5 (GitHub Packages @engenty).

commits.message:
fix(plugins): make checkPluginManifest report missing on-disk plugins

5773807 changed the runtime resolver `resolveEnabledModules` to soft-skip
manifest plugins that aren't on disk (so open worktrees listing closed
plugins still boot). checkPluginManifest delegated to it and thus stopped
reporting missing plugins, failing its test in CI (green locally only because
the environment dist was stale). Validate independently — strict, mirroring
scripts/check-engenty-plugins.mjs — instead of delegating to the lenient
runtime resolver.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(modules): package each module as a self-contained tarball (Level A / A1)

Add a per-module .npmignore so every module under modules/ is pnpm pack-able
and complete. Verified across all 27 module packages: pack is clean (no
tests/dev/__tests__/.turbo) and complete (server entry src/plugin.ts, ai/
assets where the manifest declares capabilities.ai, supabase/migrations where
migrationsDir is set).

Key finding driving the blacklist-not-whitelist choice: the platform loads a
module's server + AI face from SOURCE via jiti at runtime, including in prod
(manifest.ts resolves ./src/plugin.ts, loader.ts jiti()s it; defineModuleAi
scans ai/agents + ai/skills by path relative to the registrar's runtime
location). AI assets (agent.json, SKILL.md) are never emitted to dist/, so a
build-only or files-whitelist package would silently drop the AI face and
per-module root files (e.g. tasks/task-status-builtins.ts). dist/ still ships
(UI app consumes ./ui/plugin via the package export).

publishConfig/registry is deferred to A5 (no registry convention established
yet). See PLAN-module-packaging.md Phase A1.

commits.message:
feat(notifications): make the email notifier source-agnostic

The unread-after-delay email channel was hard-scoped to team-chat
(`source = 'team-chat'`). Generalize it to any per-user inbox record via
an operator allowlist `ENGENTY_EMAIL_NOTIFICATION_SOURCES` (comma-separated;
`*` = all sources; default `team-chat` so existing installs are unchanged).
Any producer calling `emitInboxNotification({ source, ... })` — agents,
tasks, heartbeats — can be opted in without code.

Env names generalized to `ENGENTY_EMAIL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED` /
`ENGENTY_EMAIL_NOTIFICATION_DELAY_MINUTES`, with the old `…_TEAM_CHAT_…`
names honored as a fallback. Email copy neutralized (source-neutral body).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
chore(dev): auto-restore tty after Turbo TUI in dev:portless

Keep "ui": "tui" but make an interrupted run harmless: snapshot the tty
state before launching Turbo and restore it on exit via a trap, so a
crashed or Ctrl-C'd TUI session can no longer leave the shell in raw
"staircase" mode. Falls back to `stty sane` if the snapshot is empty.
Dropped `exec` so the shell outlives Turbo to run the trap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: pass SUPABASE_DB_URL + VAPID keys to engenty-ai
commits.body:
The AI service's env block never mapped SUPABASE_DB_URL, so in prod the
Mastra store (and thus the platform inbox + the web-push/email
notification pg pools) had no Postgres connection — the inbox fell back
to in-memory and the notification channels were inert. Map it through
(same ${..:-} pattern as the other Supabase vars), plus the web-push
VAPID keys (VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY / VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY / VAPID_SUBJECT; unset =
push channel off). Documented in deploy/.env.example. No image rebuild
needed — these are runtime env for the prebuilt engenty-ai image.

manifest + SW registration already existed, so iOS home-screen installs
get push too.

commits.message:
test: Playwright smoke lane over the real stack (e2e/smoke + CI workflow)

pnpm test:smoke drives the rendered UI against the full dev stack
(playwright.config.ts webServer boots/reuses pnpm dev). Specs: shell
navigation, tasks create→delete (task-actions menu), projects
create→open→delete (row selection), contacts create, team-chat post into
a dedicated smoke-e2e channel (never real channels — they may be
Slack-bridged), copilot chat gated behind ENGENTY_SMOKE_LLM=1.

Conventions (e2e/helpers.ts): per-spec login via /auth/agent-login
(gotoLoggedIn — shared storageState breaks under refresh-token rotation),
dual-locale t()/tLoose() label matching (dev tenant may run DE or EN),
uniquely named entities deleted through the UI.

Two product fixes the lane surfaced in the agent-login path:
- dev-login /session no longer resets the password on every call
  (updateUserById revokes all sessions — concurrent logins killed each
  other's fresh sessions; now sign-in first, ensure user only on failure)
- agent-login page is single-flight (React StrictMode ran two concurrent
  mint+setSession flows that raced each other's refresh)

CI: .github/workflows/smoke.yml (nightly + workflow_dispatch; report
artifact on failure). Promote to a release gate after a clean streak.

guaranteed that no cold build ever finished — and the turbo cache never
seeded, keeping every run cold. Main runs now queue (newest queued run
supersedes intermediate ones); PRs keep the cancel behavior.

commits.message:
fix(team-chat): Slack bridge skips non-autonomous connections instead of erroring

The bridge runs autonomously (service principal), so the connections
policy denies every action when the connection's autonomous_mode is
"off" — which surfaced as a confusing "1 error" on sync. runInboundSync
now reads each bound connection's autonomous_mode up front and skips
"off" connections (new `skipped` counter in the sync summary + op
output), mirroring the inbox sync's autonomous_off handling. The
settings hint and the Connect Slack doc now state the setup explicitly:
set the connection to Autonomous mode "Full" and the write actions to
"Allow". Adds bridge.test.ts covering the skip vs. read paths.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(team-chat): email notifications via the tenant's connector (N4)

New email channel on the N1 inbox fan-out: a 60s scan in apps/ai picks
team-chat notifications still pending after a configurable delay
(default 5 min) and mails them to the recipient (core.users email)
through the tenant's own Gmail connection via the gmail_send_message
gateway op on the service JWT — per the decision to send through tenant
connectors, not a platform SMTP env. Policy applies: the connection
needs autonomous "Full" and send_message on "Allow". Without a Gmail
connection the run is a quiet no-op; send outcomes are terminal per
record (metadata.email_sent) so failures don't retry every minute, and
read-sync means anything read in time never emails. Kill-switch
ENGENTY_TEAM_CHAT_EMAIL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED, delay via
ENGENTY_TEAM_CHAT_EMAIL_DELAY_MINUTES.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(team-chat): Slack bridge (pro) — outbound replay, inbound sync, binding ops

New pro provider modules/team-chat/providers/slack-bridge (CLOSED prefix
in both publish scripts): mirrors bound conversations to a remote Slack
workspace through the connections Slack connector. Outbound rides the
module-bus message events with per-conversation ordering — post/update
replay with author prefix, markdown↔mrkdwn + mention-token mapping
(code-span safe, user_map with @Name fallback), slack ts recorded in
messages.external.slack; reaction-churn updates and deletes stay local.
Inbound is a pull sync per bound conversation over get_channel_history
(cursor in the binding, 5-min in-process interval + manual sync op),
importing through the open DAL as attributed bot posts so ts identity,
rollups and events match local messages. Loop guards: imported marker in
metadata (atomic at post) + known-slack-ts dedup. Management ops:
team_chat_slack_status/bind/unbind/bound_list/sync_run.

Open module changes (additive): PostMessageRecord.botId passthrough,
service posts allowed with botId, ./dal export subpath, Slack connector
mapMessage passes subtype through.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(team-chat): user notifications — mention/DM fan-out into the platform inbox (N1)

Posted messages (user and agent authored) enqueue one pgmq
team_chat_notification dispatch with targets computed module-side:
mentions and @here/@channel notify always, DM members by default,
thread participants on replies, notify_prefs.level="all" opts into
channel activity; muted and level="nothing" silence, authors and
agents are never targeted. The apps/ai consumer (kill-switch
ENGENTY_TEAM_CHAT_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED) writes one inbox record per
target onto the per-user partition inbox:{tenant}:{user} — the layer
the inbox module anticipated; the /ai/v1/notifications routes now
merge the team + user threads via the caller's scope. Read-sync:
conversations.mark enqueues a read dispatch that flips pending records
for now-read messages to seen. The desktop bridge renders team-chat
records natively (channel label + author + preview) from the
structured payload and polls with background refetch so a hidden/tray
window still notifies.

commits.message:
fix(deps): pin @hookform/resolvers to the consumer's zod via packageExtensions

The resolver has no zod peer dependency, so its zod type imports resolved
through pnpm's hidden hoist fallback — and the team-chat dependency
additions flipped that hoist winner from zod 4 to zod 3, breaking the
zodResolver overloads in every form package. Declaring zod as an optional
peer makes pnpm link the resolver against each consumer's own zod,
independent of hoist order.

commits.message:
fix(desktop): resolve API/AI base URLs lazily + surface uncaught errors in the shell

The desktop shell installs runtime env overrides after the module graph
evaluates; the module-scope env snapshot in apps/ui config froze the empty
build-time values, so workspace/api calls went same-origin to
tauri://localhost, whose SPA fallback answered every path with index.html —
the context 'response' was an HTML string and the authenticated shell
crashed to a white window (resolvedAppearance.font on undefined).

Also add a desktop-only error overlay (window error + unhandledrejection)
so future shell crashes are diagnosable without devtools.

commits.message:
fix(copilot): thread-scope the composer message queue and clear it on stop

Part of the run/resume 409 wedge fix. Bind the client message queue to the
active thread (resets on thread switch / "New chat" so a queued message can no
longer replay into an unrelated thread), gate auto-drain while an approval
interrupt is open, and clear the queue on Stop so a stopped/wedged run does not
leave messages parked to auto-send.

row actions), while literal/objectRef surfaces kept rendering:

1. The root pnpm `"zod": "4.4.3"` override forced the whole @a2ui stack
   (and @engenty/a2ui-catalog) onto zod 4, but the A2UI binder introspects
   schemas via zod-3 internals (`_def.typeName`). Under zod 4 it recognizes
   nothing, so actions never become dispatch closures and `{path}` bindings
   never resolve. Scope the a2ui packages back to zod 3 via nested overrides.

2. The catalog now dispatches actions defensively (not relying on the binder
   resolving them), and must hand `dispatchAction` the whole
   `{ event: { name, context } }` payload — it reads `payload.event`. The
   handler had unwrapped one level too far, so the dispatch silently no-op'd.

Adds a binder-contract test asserting the schema still scrapes action→ACTION
and dynamic→DYNAMIC, so a future zod-version drift fails loudly. Verified
live: the show_ui "Details" button opens the offer in the pane.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: thread-scope the composer message queue and clear it on stop
commits.body:
Part of the run/resume 409 wedge fix. Bind the client message queue to the
active thread (resets on thread switch / "New chat" so a queued message can no
longer replay into an unrelated thread), gate auto-drain while an approval
interrupt is open, and clear the queue on Stop so a stopped/wedged run does not
leave messages parked to auto-send.

commits.message: dock queue + approval surfaces as a flap attached to the composer
commits.body:
Queue (Warteschlange) and approval/decision/feedback banners no longer render
as a separate gapped block above the composer. They thread through
dockedInterruptSurface -> CopilotPanelComposerBlock.dockedSurface -> new
CopilotCompactComposerShell.dockContent and render as an in-flow flap tucked
directly behind the composer card: card background, rounded top, the card
overlaps the flap bottom (-mb-5 / pb-7) so there is no gap. In-flow (not
absolute) so variable-height content pushes the transcript up instead of
covering it.

The blob avatar renders inside the flap and rides its top edge instead of
overlapping the row controls; the queue surface drops its own muted box chrome
and the pr-16 blob inset; the drawer body drops its now-redundant padding
wrapper; the status flap is suppressed while dock content is shown.

docs(wip): generative-ui — adjudicate the MCP-Apps-vs-A2UI challenge per use case

MCP Apps wins external widgets (shipped, ecosystem default) and arbitrary
generated one-offs (beyond-catalog expressiveness, sandbox stronger than
validation for generated code). It is structurally incapable of the primary
ask — composing our core UI elements with objects by reference — because an
iframe cannot host the app's React components, theme, query cache or
live-cache loop. Division of labor stands: A2UI leads internal composition,
MCP Apps keeps the external + arbitrary rails; internal MCP Apps widgets
noted as the knowing fallback if catalog+renderer proves heavy.

feat(team-chat): Phase 3 — agents as first-class participants

Agent mentions dispatch real agent runs: <@agent:key> mentions in
post_message enqueue onto the new team_chat_agent_mention pgmq queue
(best-effort, never fails the post); a new apps/ai consumer resolves the
service scope, builds thread context via ops, runs the agent headless
(runDelegatedConversation, stable per-thread ai.thread id for memory),
and posts the reply back via the new team_chat_post_as_agent op —
agent-authored (member agents or public channels; never impersonates a
user) — recording agent_thread_links.

AI tools via defineModuleAi (team_chat_list_channels / read_thread /
post) give every agent sanctioned channel access. Composer mention
popover now lists registry agents (same-origin fallback for the registry
fetch); agent messages render with an AGENT badge and a View-agent-run
link to the copilot thread. Kill-switch:
ENGENTY_TEAM_CHAT_MENTIONS_ENABLED.

commits.message: productionize widget host — bridge, CSP, template cache
commits.body:
Phase C: the server client now resolves declared ui:// templates
(per-server cache, 1MB cap, csp + structuredContent passthrough) and no
longer fabricates demo HTML when a tool declares no widget. The chat card
renders widgets through a postMessage JSON-RPC host frame (ui/initialize
handshake, tool-input/result push, size-changed, open-link, display-mode)
with a host-injected CSP built from the resource's declared domains.

authenticated per user and validated against the tenant's registered MCP
servers.

commits.message:
feat(secrets): agent-gated reveals — identity forwarding, approval gate, durable goal grants

Close the silent-bypass hole where a copilot chat could decrypt any secret the
signed-in user could reveal, unaudited and unapproved, because agent identity
never reached core.

- Provision a core.agents security principal per AI agent: mapping column
  ai.engenty_ai_agents.core_agent_id (registry agents) + find-or-create by
  (tenant, name) for builtins, race-safe via unique index (migration
  20260719120000). ensureCoreAgentId is idempotent; verified against the local
  stack (apps/ai/scripts/verify-core-agent-link.ts).
- Forward x-engenty-agent-id / x-engenty-goal-id (goal = conversation thread)
  from every run context: conversation start/resume, generate path, delegated
  children (own identity, inherited goal), and voice.
- Widen PluginAuthContext with agentId/goalId; secrets_reveal now detects
  agent-ness from ctx.auth and audits the AGENT principal with the real
  goal_id (decrypt_for_agent) instead of mis-attributing to the user.
- Approving a gated reveal persists a durable goal-scoped grant: the approval
  artifact id carries {secret_id} (uuid only, never raw tool input); the
  approve hook and the voice execute path call the new module endpoint
  POST /api/secrets/:id/goal-grants, which enforces the approver's own reveal
  ceiling before upserting core.agent_goal_grants (agent_id null,
  capability secrets.read:<id>) — before the resume re-invokes core.

Verified against the live local stack: agent invoke 202 approval_required →
grant → 200 with correct audit row; wrong goal re-gates; non-owner approver
403 (no grant); plain user path unchanged. Chat-UX halves pending a valid
AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY (docs/wip/secrets-agent-gate-test-plan.md).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: agent-gated reveals — identity forwarding, approval gate, durable goal grants
commits.body:
Close the silent-bypass hole where a copilot chat could decrypt any secret the
signed-in user could reveal, unaudited and unapproved, because agent identity
never reached core.

- Provision a core.agents security principal per AI agent: mapping column
  ai.engenty_ai_agents.core_agent_id (registry agents) + find-or-create by
  (tenant, name) for builtins, race-safe via unique index (migration
  20260719120000). ensureCoreAgentId is idempotent; verified against the local
  stack (apps/ai/scripts/verify-core-agent-link.ts).
- Forward x-engenty-agent-id / x-engenty-goal-id (goal = conversation thread)
  from every run context: conversation start/resume, generate path, delegated
  children (own identity, inherited goal), and voice.
- Widen PluginAuthContext with agentId/goalId; secrets_reveal now detects
  agent-ness from ctx.auth and audits the AGENT principal with the real
  goal_id (decrypt_for_agent) instead of mis-attributing to the user.
- Approving a gated reveal persists a durable goal-scoped grant: the approval
  artifact id carries {secret_id} (uuid only, never raw tool input); the
  approve hook and the voice execute path call the new module endpoint
  POST /api/secrets/:id/goal-grants, which enforces the approver's own reveal
  ceiling before upserting core.agent_goal_grants (agent_id null,
  capability secrets.read:<id>) — before the resume re-invokes core.

Verified against the live local stack: agent invoke 202 approval_required →
grant → 200 with correct audit row; wrong goal re-gates; non-owner approver
403 (no grant); plain user path unchanged. Chat-UX halves pending a valid
AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY (docs/wip/secrets-agent-gate-test-plan.md).

commits.message: client-anchored secrets vault + services module
commits.body:
New `secrets` module and `@engenty/secrets-sdk` for a password/secrets
manager anchored to clients (org-contacts), scoped user/project/client/
tenant, with paid-services registry — the engenty port of engrdian's
vault, minus its flaws (see docs/wip/secrets-vault-module.md).

- Server-side AES-256-GCM with AAD binding ciphertext to row identity
  (anti-swap); ciphertext columns never granted to `authenticated`.
- resolve.ts: single authority for "can principal read secret X" —
  owner-scope membership (client access flows through project teams) +
  explicit/goal grants; agents never inherit scope.
- Agent reveal gated by createSecretsRevealPolicy (R10: agent identity
  lives only in the profile-policy layer, not the operation handler).
- Verified: SDK unit tests (crypto AAD + resolve truth table), live DB
  round-trip, and a full create->reveal driven through the app UI.

commits.message:
perf(deploy): split pnpm install via pnpm fetch to fix Docker layer caching

The deps stage in Dockerfile.ai/edge copied full source (apps/packages/modules)
before `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, so ANY source change invalidated the
install layer and forced a full network dependency re-resolve on every build —
even though only lockfile changes should require that.

`pnpm fetch` resolves + downloads into the local store from the lockfile alone
(no source needed), so it now stays cached across source-only changes; the
subsequent `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` after the full-source
copy becomes a fast local link instead of a network fetch.

Verified locally: full docker build succeeds and runs (deps + build + runtime
stages for both Dockerfiles), and a source-only edit leaves the `pnpm fetch`
layer CACHED while install drops to ~10s.

commits.message: calendar pull-back / two-way sync (Phase 3)
commits.body:
Google-only incremental pull-back of remote calendar changes onto linked
time entries:
- gcal list_events gains sync_token/return_sync_token, returns
  next_sync_token, handles 410-expiry (sync_token_expired) with a
  full-window re-list, drains pages, and exposes event 'updated'.
- pullConnection reconciles remote → local: match by provider_event_id,
  newer-wins via updated_at vs event.updated, loop prevention via
  sync_hash re-stamp, remote cancellation -> link status remote_deleted
  (entry preserved), foreign/all-day events never create entries.
- reconcile op pulls Google connections before pushing; run response
  gains pulled/unlinked counts. Cursor reuses the existing
  calendar_sync_state.cursor column (no new migration).

commits.message:
feat(ai-ui): file & photo upload in chat composer (all surfaces)

Wire the existing (but inert) attachment UI end-to-end so users can attach
photos/PDFs/files in every chat surface, see them as chips, send them, and have
images + PDFs reach the model (vision) while any file lands in the Vault.

- Layer 1: `uploadChatAttachment*` — browser-direct signed-URL upload into the
  `files` bucket under `tenants/<id>/chat/…`; self-contained in ai-ui.
- Layer 2: composer renders attachment chips (both compact + full layouts),
  uploads on submit, and threads AG-UI content parts through submitMessage;
  attachment-only sends are allowed.
- Layer 3: transcript renders image thumbnails / file chips, re-deriving fresh
  signed URLs from the durable storage key so previews survive reload.
- Layer 4: run route stops flattening the turn to text — extracts attachment
  parts, resolves model-feedable MIME (image/*, application/pdf) to base64 via
  the core file-storage client, and forwards them to session.sendMessage(files).

Storage-backed transport keeps base64 out of the messages table. Adds en/de
strings and unit tests for the part contract + backend extraction.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(chat-upload): feed model + persist attachments; AI SDK tile variants

Two functional bugs found via live testing, plus the composer/transcript
redesign to match the AI SDK Elements Attachments patterns.

Bug 1 — model never saw the image. resolveModelAttachments() required a
coreBaseUrl, but createApp() boots without one in prod, so it silently
returned []. Fall back to getEngentyCoreBaseUrlFromEnv() (same source the
rest of apps/ai uses).

Bug 2 — attachments vanished on reload. Mastra persists the user turn as
text-only (the base64 files it's handed feed the model but aren't durable
parts). Thread the raw AG-UI image/document parts (latestUserAttachmentParts)
through startConversationRun into the per-run memory storage, which folds
them onto the first persisted user message (one-shot; the insert wins via
ignoreDuplicates). On reload the transcript re-derives a fresh signed URL
from the stored storageKey.

UI — new shared AttachmentImageTile (grid variant, square thumbnail) and
AttachmentFileBadge (inline variant, icon+name pill). Composer and transcript
both render images first (grid) then files (inline), matching
elements.ai-sdk.dev/components/attachments.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(chat-upload): resolve coreBaseUrl fallback, durable attachment persistence, and Gateway file-part encoding

- resolveModelAttachments now falls back to getEngentyCoreBaseUrlFromEnv() when
  coreBaseUrl isn't passed explicitly (createApp() boots without it) — model was
  silently never receiving images.
- Fold durable AG-UI image/document parts onto the first persisted user message
  in EngentySessionMemoryStorage, replacing Mastra's auto-generated inline-base64
  file parts; filter attachment parts back out of Mastra's recall path so stored
  images don't break subsequent-turn prompt assembly.
- Add gatewayFileDataMiddleware: normalizes file-part data to the AI SDK v4
  {type:"data", data:<base64 string>} shape, which survives the Gateway wire
  schema and avoids maybeEncodeFileParts rewriting it into a data: URL that
  Google Vertex rejects as an invalid fileUri.

feat(copilot): prefer artifacts for documents; bound frontend-tool interrupts

- AGENTS.md: steer the agent to artifact_create/update/show_artifact for
  documents the user reads/edits (markdown/html/table), reserving
  offer_file_downloads for files to save/hand off; clarify keys must be
  tenant storage keys, not /sandbox paths.
- Frontend-tool interrupts get a 3-minute TTL (agUiOpenInterruptTtlMsForKind)
  instead of the 7-day decision-interrupt default.

  settles (missing/hung executor) now resumes with a 'couldn't resolve' tool
  failure instead of leaving the run suspended indefinitely.

commits.message:
fix(release): raise git-cliff maxBuffer to avoid ENOBUFS

The `cliff --context` call that regenerates changelog.json emits the full
structured JSON for every commit since the last tag, which exceeds
execFileSync's 1 MB default buffer and throws ENOBUFS on long histories
(breaking `pnpm release` / `pnpm release:changelog`). Set maxBuffer to 256 MB.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: raise git-cliff maxBuffer to avoid ENOBUFS
commits.body:
The `cliff --context` call that regenerates changelog.json emits the full
structured JSON for every commit since the last tag, which exceeds
execFileSync's 1 MB default buffer and throws ENOBUFS on long histories
(breaking `pnpm release` / `pnpm release:changelog`). Set maxBuffer to 256 MB.

commits.message: serialize parallel tool-approval suspensions and resume reliably
commits.body:
Multiple approval-gated tool calls in one step re-asked the same permission
and could wedge the run with no terminal event. Suspensions now queue so
each approval card appears once, resume validation accepts the remaining
open interrupts, and grants persist across the resume cycle.

commits.message:
fix(ci): keep public repo workflows untouched in open-source snapshot

The snapshot replaced the public mirror's tree wholesale, so every publish
tried to create/update/delete .github/workflows/* on engenty/engenty. The
Contents-scoped PUBLIC_REPO_PUSH_TOKEN can't touch workflow files (no
`workflow` scope), so the push was rejected ("refusing to allow a Personal
Access Token to create or update workflow ..."). Mirror the public branch's
own .github/workflows/ tree into the snapshot so those paths never diff;
the public repo's CI is managed directly on the mirror.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

A Claude Code worktree (.claude/worktrees/agent-session-flows) was
committed as a submodule gitlink (mode 160000) with no .gitmodules entry,
so actions/checkout@v4's `git submodule foreach` step fails with
"No url found for submodule path" — breaking CI and the publish-open
workflow. Remove the gitlink and gitignore .claude/worktrees/.

commits.message:
feat(time-tracking): push time entries to calendar (Phase 2)

Two-way-ready push sync: scheduled time entries are written to a chosen
Google Calendar as events, with a stable id mapping in both directions.

- schema: module_time_tracking.calendar_links (entry ⇄ event, unique on
  provider event id, survives entry deletion for orphan cleanup) and
  calendar_sync_state (per-connection enable/target/time_zone/cursor).
- gcal connector: create/update_event accept private_properties
  (extendedProperties.private, stamping engenty_entry_id) and a time_zone
  (wall-clock + IANA zone, DST-safe); event summaries return etag.
- calendar-sync-service: pushTimeEntry (create/update/delete remote per link
  state, sync_hash skips redundant writes) + syncConnection reconcile
  (backfill unlinked scheduled entries, repair errors, delete orphans).
- in-request push: create/update/move/delete fire pushTimeEntry as the live
  user (best-effort, never fails the write).
- reconcile op time_tracking_calendar_sync_run + apps/ai calendar-sync
  system job (*/15). Runs as service principal (needs autonomous_mode:full).
- ui: "Sync my hours" section in the Calendars menu — pick a target
  calendar + enable toggle; enabling backfills as the live user.

Not applied to any DB yet; needs a connected Google Calendar to verify E2E.
Plan: docs/wip/time-tracking-calendar-sync.md (Phase 2)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(authz): roles & capabilities authorization with member access gating

Introduce role profiles (core built-ins, per-module viewer/editor bundles, and
tenant-defined custom roles) resolved to capability strings by resolveGrants,
with DB role_assignments for users and agents and goal-scoped agent approval
escalation. Add RLS coverage across core + module tenant tables (with a CI
guard), project visibility and ownership ABAC, and a /settings/roles admin
console.

Members are scoped to end-user surfaces: personal settings (Profile, module
connections) + module apps only — no tenant configuration (General, AI models,
tenant Appearance), /admin/* consoles, developer mode, or role management.
Enforcement stays capability-based and consistent across the session,
device-flow, and API-token paths.

commits.message:
feat(deploy): apply Supabase migrations automatically on deploy

Add an engenty-migrate init service that runs `supabase db push` against
SUPABASE_DB_URL before the app starts (edge/ai depends_on it via
service_completed_successfully), so no container ever serves a stale schema.
Opt-in and non-breaking: the step skips (exit 0) when SUPABASE_DB_URL is unset,
so installs that still migrate by hand keep deploying. Builds
ghcr.io/engenty/engenty-migrate via the image matrix; SUPABASE_DB_URL gains the
deploy scope and is documented in DEPLOY.md + the wizard.

commits.message:
Add per-tab agent session binding, realtime sync, and unified status UI

Multiple browser tabs shared one localStorage-backed "active thread" per
copilot lane, so switching sessions in one tab silently retargeted every
other tab. Active-thread selection is now per-tab (sessionStorage-first,
seeded once from the shared map so a new tab inherits the last session);
the header and drawer surface which session is bound.

Same-thread tabs now stay in sync in real time: the existing per-thread

persisted timesheet rows no longer duplicate.

commits.message:
fix(time-tracking): correct today navigation and week-switch scroll reset

- goToday used Math.round on a fractional day-count (ms diff / 86400000),
  which rounds up to the next day any time after noon local — landed on
  tomorrow in day/3-day view. Use differenceInCalendarDays instead.
- the initial-scroll-to-08:00 effect only ever ran once (a boolean ref),
  so navigating weeks/spans left the grid scrolled to 00:00. Re-key it on
  the visible day range (weekStart + span) so it resets on navigation but
  not on a weekend expand/collapse.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
ci: auto-publish open subset to public repo on release tags

The public engenty/engenty mirror lagged behind releases (manual, easy to
forget). Add publish-open.yml: on every v* tag, snapshot-publish the open
subset to the public repo via a new reusable script,
scripts/publish-open-snapshot.sh (also `pnpm push:snapshot`).

The script replaces the public branch tree with origin/main minus the
closed/pro-only paths (Manage, banking, brand-assets, licensed fonts, and
the deploy workflow), with a safety check that refuses to push if any
excluded path leaks. Requires a PUBLIC_REPO_PUSH_TOKEN secret.

commits.message:
ci(deploy): path-filter image builds to only rebuild what changed

Every push to main rebuilt all three images (edge/ai/sandbox), even for
docs/README/single-app changes. Add a `changes` job (dorny/paths-filter)
that computes a dynamic build matrix from each image's real inputs:

- edge    → root manifests, scripts, packages, modules, apps/core, apps/ui
- ai      → root manifests, scripts, packages, modules, apps/ai
- sandbox → deploy/Dockerfile.sandbox only (image copies no repo source,
  so it was rebuilding every push for nothing)

A workflow change still rebuilds everything (safe default). The deploy
job now fires when any image was rebuilt OR deploy/** config (e.g. the
compose) changed, and is skipped after a failed build — so config-only
changes still redeploy and no-op pushes don't.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(env-setup): prefer legacy JWT keys for local Supabase (#2)

* fix(env-setup): prefer legacy JWT keys when harvesting local Supabase status

The wizard resolved Supabase keys new-format-first (SECRET_KEY/
PUBLISHABLE_KEY), writing sb_secret_/sb_publishable_ values to .env.local.
The local Supabase CLI stack's PostgREST only validates HS256 JWTs against
JWT_SECRET and rejects the single-part sb_* keys (PGRST301) unless
asymmetric signing keys are configured — so dev:env:init produced a stack
that 500s on every request to a custom schema.

resolveSupabaseValue now takes a preferJwt option; the wizard sets it when
harvesting from 'supabase status' (always the local stack) so the legacy
3-part JWT keys win. Production/example preference for the new keys is
unchanged.

* docs(dev): add setup-process guide and expand plugin lifecycle docs

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(catalog-search): skip embedding when no gateway credentials

The catalog search embedding path issued a live AI Gateway call even with no
credentials, then caught the auth failure and fell back to lexical. On CI
(no API key / OIDC token) and slow shared runners that doomed round-trip could
exceed the 10s test timeout, flaking apps/ai and api tests that boot the app.

Short-circuit to lexical ranking when neither AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY nor
VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN is set — behavior-equivalent (it fell back anyway) but fast
and deterministic, and quicker in any keyless environment. api-catalog tests
stub a key since they exercise the (mocked) embedding path.

fix(ci): run project setup script, not pnpm's builtin 'setup'

`pnpm setup` invokes pnpm's reserved built-in (configures PNPM_HOME), so the
project's "setup" script ('pnpm engenty setup') never ran in CI. That meant
supabase/migrations was never aggregated, so migration-reading tests
(supabase-sync-lib, live-cache) failed with ENOENT and createApp-based AI tests
hung. Use 'pnpm run setup' to invoke the package script.

This is why main's CI was red since the workflow landed.

feat(cli): plugins install — surface db migrate next-step + opt-in --db-migrate

surprised users (install OK, UI then throws "Invalid schema"). After installing
in-repo workspace modules it now prints the next step ("run pnpm db:migrate"),
and a new opt-in `--db-migrate` flag applies them locally — gated on a reachable
local DB so install stays DB-free for CI, fresh checkouts, and remote databases.

Generic, surface-keyed tab registry mirroring the existing dashboardWidgets/
settingsItems contribution chain. A module contributes a tab to another

exists while the contributing plugin is enabled, so hosts get install-gated
tabs with no feature flag or availability check on their side.

  UiEventMap ("ui.tabs"), and EngentyUiApi.registerTab
- registerTab impl + resolve emit in engenty-ui-api; normalizeTabs dedupes per
  (surface, id) and warns on collisions; stale-owner cleanup + reload pruning
- resolver/queries/context empties carry tabs; tests cover collection,
  disabled-plugin gating, and per-surface dedupe

commits.message:
fix(copilot): keep floating avatar FAB on-screen

The Copilot floating avatar (CopilotFabTrigger) applied its persisted
`fabPosition` verbatim. A position saved on a larger window rendered the
FAB off the viewport edge on a smaller one, so the avatar silently
disappeared with no recovery. The existing viewport-clamp only covered
the open floating drawer, never the collapsed FAB.

Clamp the persisted position to the current viewport when resolving the
FAB anchor (re-applied on resize) and in resolveTriggerAnchor so drag
origin and speed-dial centering match the rendered position. Also reset
collapseToCircle when the drawer is open so the two states can't conflict.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(copilot): make drawer robust before layout hydration and sidebar mount

Harden copilot surface mounting against two races:

- Gate CopilotDrawerLayer until the persisted `copilot.layout` snapshot is
  applied (`copilotLayoutApplied`) so the drawer/FAB don't render with a
  stale default position before hydration.
- Track inline-sidebar mount state (`copilotSidebarReady` +
  notifySidebarMounted/Unmounted) to re-render when the portal target
  attaches, and fall back to the drawer SidePanel when the sidebar
  container isn't available while open (extracted `renderDrawerFallback`).
- Reconcile the persisted layout snapshot via reconcileCopilotLayoutSnapshot
  before applying it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
Add --db-restart to plugins install for schema exposure

Applying a module's migrations creates its tables, but the running API
only serves schemas listed in config.toml db-schemas, read at boot — so a
newly installed module's schema stays unreachable until the stack restarts.

Add an opt-in --db-restart flag (pair with --db-migrate) and an engenty
db restart subcommand that stop/starts the local stack so PostgREST
reloads the exposed schemas. Gated on a reachable local database, matching
the existing --db-migrate opt-in.

commits.message:
Add adoption docs: memory, approvals, file-based agents, Code Mode

Four focused docs/wip analyses against @mastra/core 1.48:
- memory: only lastMessages is used today; adoption order for title
  generation, resource-scope working memory (adapter already carries the
  field), tool-call filter/token limiter processors, and Observational
  Memory via pg-delegated OM record storage; semantic recall skipped in
  favor of OM retrieval.
- approvals: converge the four HITL mechanisms onto native
  suspend/resume - the 1.48 input-aware requireApproval predicate can
  gate per operation, so the abort-and-rerun decision-artifact flow can
  be deleted; contracts/grants remain the policy source; suspended runs
  survive restarts via the pg workflows domain.
- file-based agents: keep the defineModuleAi convention (superset);
  adopt createSkill; note the pure assembleAgentFromFsEntry seam.
- Code Mode: generate typed per-operation tools from the contract
  catalog, read-only allow-list first on the task specialist, writes
  stay outside Code Mode.

look (Apple menu convention: padded tray, smaller-radius rows floating
inside it).

commits.message:
Contribute a Files tab to the project-detail page

The projects module already exposed a plugin extension point for this
(PROJECTS_DETAIL_SURFACE + registerTab, see use-project-tabs.ts) so that
projects has no hard dependency on files-ui — but the files module's side
of the contract was never implemented, so the tab never appeared. Legacy
had the same feature, just wired as a hard workspace dependency instead
(projects imported FileManager directly).

Adds ProjectFilesTab, which reads {projectId, viewMode} from the tab's
params and mounts the already-built FileManager component scoped to
{type: 'project', id: projectId} — the file-manager-store DAL already
supports arbitrary owner scoping, this just needed a consumer. Threads
viewMode through project-detail-page's contributed-tab params so the tab
respects the project's external/read-only view like legacy did.

The tab is opt-in via the existing tab configurator (not auto-enabled),
consistent with how every other tab in that dialog behaves.

commits.message:
Extract Select's glass background into a shared .ui-canvas-glass class

The glass variant's background+blur was hardcoded inline in select.tsx's
cva config, so DropdownMenu/Popover/HoverCard couldn't reuse it without
copy-pasting the Tailwind string. Add .ui-canvas-glass to
ui-canvas-chrome.css as a sibling of the existing .ui-canvas-floating,
same pattern, so any floating surface can opt in later.

Scoped to background + backdrop-filter only (no box-shadow): a plain CSS
box-shadow in that class does NOT compose with Tailwind's ring-*/shadow-*
utilities — both set the box-shadow property outright, so whichever
cascades last wins and the other is silently dropped. Discovered this
after the glass variant's ring-1 was clobbering .ui-canvas-glass's own
box-shadow entirely (verified via computed styles: only the ring layer
survived, the elevation shadow vanished). Shadow/ring/radius stay as
Tailwind utilities per consumer so they keep composing correctly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
Fix copilot voice call races and duplicate FAB surface

Two issues in the realtime voice session:
- OpenAI refuses response.create while a response is already in flight
  (conversation_already_has_active_response) — queue the request instead
  of sending it immediately after a tool-call result, flush on the next
  response.done.
- That error (and response_cancel_not_active) left the data channel and
  audio fully usable, but the hook was tearing down the whole session on
  any 'error' status — now only genuinely fatal errors end the call.

Also: the voice FAB and a floating call-strip composer override could
both be visible at once (e.g. shell reports closed while a call strip is
mounted) — track call-strip presence via CopilotVoiceProvider and hide
the FAB while one is mounted, so there's a single voice surface.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

survived, the elevation shadow vanished). Shadow/ring/radius stay as
Tailwind utilities per consumer so they keep composing correctly.

commits.message:
Add the deploy/ bundle for VPS/Coolify deployment

Ports the full deployment bundle the public docs already reference
(docs/content/setup/coolify.md, deploy/.env.example header): a Compose
stack served through a single engenty-edge gateway (port 8787) plus the
engenty-ai runtime, with optional docs/studio/sandbox images.

- docker-compose.yml, DEPLOY.md, scripts/migrate.sh, and
  Dockerfile.{edge,ai,docs,studio,sandbox} + .dockerignore.
- apps/manage is closed-source and excluded: the gateway's /manage route
  defaults off (ENGENTY_GATEWAY_MANAGE_ENABLED=false) in both compose and
  the edge image, so open builds need no admin portal.
- Runtime images ship the workspace packages/ + modules/ trees and each
  app's own node_modules so pnpm's symlinked workspace deps resolve at
  boot; TURBO_BUILD_CONCURRENCY caps parallelism on small builders.
- Removes the "not yet included" status callout (and now-inaccurate
  /manage references) from the Coolify guide.

Verified: both images build and boot; edge serves /api + / and returns
the intended 404 on /manage; engenty-ai reports healthy on /ai/health;
deploy/.env.example matches the env manifest (env:example:check passes).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
Move API-catalog semantic search from apps/core to apps/ai

Core keeps catalog building and its gateway method but ranks lexically
only (drops the ai package + embedding calls; no AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
needed in core). apps/ai now applies the full ranking on the agent path:
shared lexical BM25 (extracted to @engenty/search-index) plus semantic
embedding reranking with lexical fallback, over the tenant-gated
contracts fetched from core. Contract sources are pluggable
(CatalogContractSource) so external API catalogs can merge into the same
ranked catalog later; a 60s per-bearer cache fronts the core fetch.

commits.message:
fix(copilot): dock floating launcher & avatar to bottom-right on mode switch

The floating compact launcher was positioned from floatingPosition, whose
default was sized to the modal (FLOATING_DEFAULT_HEIGHT=148) while the launcher
renders at ~56px — so switching to floating dropped it mid-screen, and nothing
re-cornered either surface on mode changes.

- Size the launcher's bottom-right home to its own footprint via
  resolveLauncherCornerPosition (used for the initial position too).
- Re-dock both surfaces to the corner when switching to floating/mini-floating
  from the position menu (launcher via floatingPosition, avatar via clearing
  fabPosition/anchor).
- Add a floatingDockedToCorner flag + layout effect that keeps the resting
  launcher pinned as its measured height settles; cleared once the user drags.
- reanchorFloatingPositionToViewport keeps a corner-docked panel tracking its
  edges on window resize instead of only clamping.

Verified in-app: switch->floating, switch->avatar, and reload all land
bottom-right; window resize tracks the corner.

commits.message:
Replace the routine scheduler with Triggers backed by Mastra heartbeats

A Trigger is the single model for 'a reason work starts' (schedule |
event | manual) and always references a task template — firing a
trigger materializes a Task into the durable task pipeline. There are
no prompt-only routines.

- tasks module: module_tasks.triggers + task_templates (schema, DAL,
  gateway operations incl. triggers_fire as the one execution path
  shared by scheduled, manual, and future event fires).
- apps/ai src/scheduler/: Mastra heartbeats as the pure cron substrate.
  The prepare hook enforces quiet hours, fires the trigger via the
  service principal, and returns null so no agent ever runs; a no-op
  engenty.scheduler agent anchors the heartbeats (worker requirement).
  Reconcile syncs module ROUTINE.md declarations -> trigger rows ->
  heartbeats at boot (deferred: the module capability loader blocks
  during createApp) and on demand via POST /ai/v1/triggers/reconcile.
- /ai/v1/triggers routes replace /ai/v1/routines; system jobs
  (cleanup-interrupts) ride their own heartbeats; the pg_cron tick,
  due.ts cron parsing, ai.routine_state and ai.custom_routine are
  dropped (core migration). cron-parser dependency removed — Engenty
  parses no cron anymore.
- routines UI now speaks the trigger API: single schedule per routine,
  task-template payloads (name doubles as task title, instructions as
  task description).
- fix: the Session workspace fallback from the 1.48 migration threw at
  runtime ('Workspace requires at least a filesystem, sandbox, or
  skills') on runs without a workspace, e.g. headless task jobs — now a
  shared scratch-dir LocalFilesystem workspace that feeds no tools.

Validated live: trigger created via UI and API -> heartbeat row ->
minute-cron fire -> task materialized with correct template fields ->
dispatch consumer -> task-job workflow -> specialist run -> in_review;
enable/disable pause-resume, delete removes the heartbeat, boot
reconcile recreates system-job heartbeats.

commits.message:
Converge tool approvals onto native Mastra suspend/resume

Replace the abort-and-rerun decision-artifact approval flow with native
tool-level suspend/resume: engenty_tool_execute declares suspend/resume
schemas and suspends the run when a contract requires approval. The
Approve/Deny decision resumes the SAME parked run in place via
respondToToolSuspension — no re-run, no lost turn.

- approvalPolicy on the engenty-tools run context (suspend | deny |
  artifact; default deny, fail-safe): interactive chat suspends,
  delegated leaf runs deny (would deadlock the parent), voice keeps its
  artifact + /v1/realtime/tools/approve flow.
- Tool-approval interrupts persist as decision-kind open interrupts
  carrying the suspended run_id; the runs route routes them to the
  parked-session resume (not the artifact re-run branch), folds the
  Approve once/always grant into session metadata, and audits the
  decision. The write-back on interrupt-clear carries the just-persisted
  grant so it survives the resume.
- resumeConversationRun drives the continuation inside the engenty-tools
  ALS context so a second gated call in the continuation suspends again
  instead of being denied, with persisted grants threaded through.
- Full-page copilot chat: fall back to the persisted open interrupt when
  the transcript has no decision artifact to render (the suspended tool
  call has no result), matching the drawer.
- Restart recovery via listSuspendedRuns is deferred; parked sessions
  keep the frontend-tool 15-min TTL (documented in docs/wip).

commits.message:
Guard engenty_tool_execute against empty tool-call input

Some models/providers drop function-call arguments entirely (observed
100% reproducible with minimax/minimax-m3: every engenty_tool_execute
call arrives with input {}). The empty input previously reached core and
surfaced as a raw zod validation error the model retried verbatim.

- Reject an empty input object before the approval gate when the
  operation contract declares required fields, with a factual message
  naming the missing fields and the likely cause (the current model's
  function calling) so the agent reports it to the user instead of
  looping on validation errors. Never asks for approval on a doomed call.
- Give the execute tool's input field a real object schema
  (z.record) instead of z.unknown(), which serialized to an empty JSON
  schema in the tool definition. (Verified this alone does not fix
  MiniMax — the arguments are dropped provider-side — but the tool
  definition is now correct for schema-strict providers.)

commits.message:
Show the voice approval dialog in threadless voice sessions

A voice session started on a fresh chat has no active thread, and the
voice provider only parked a gated backend op's approval for the
confirmation dialog when a thread existed — without one, the raw
decision artifact went back to the voice model, which then narrated an

re-invoke as a one-shot approval_grant_once on the execute call — the
same authority as the persisted-grant path (an explicit user decision on
the user's own bearer token), scoped to that single call.

commits.message:
Add event triggers: module-event bus + webhook ingestion onto triggers_fire

Phase 2 of the trigger cutover — event triggers fire the same
triggers_fire task materialization as schedule and manual triggers,
through two ingestion edges:

- provider_id 'module-events': the tasks plugin subscribes to the
  in-process plugin event bus (engenty.events.modules) for every
  canonical event name an enabled trigger listens to (exact-name
  subscriptions, replayed from the database on boot, extended on
  trigger create/update), applies the shallow event_filter payload
  match, and fires per matching tenant trigger.
- provider_id 'webhook': a public tasks-module route
  POST /api/tasks/trigger-hooks/:triggerId/:secret, authenticated by a
  per-trigger secret generated at creation (timing-safe compare, one
  generic 401 for every reject reason).

Both edges attach the event payload to the materialized task's
description so the agent works on the concrete occurrence. The fire
logic is extracted from the triggers_fire gateway op into a shared
fireTrigger (scoped to the trigger row's own tenant/scope), used by all
callers including the heartbeat hook path.

Mastra SignalProviders are deliberately NOT used: compiled-dist
verification showed they are thread-scoped (every subscription is a
(resourceId, threadId), delivery is sendNotificationSignal into a
thread, the documented POST /api/signals/:providerId route does not
exist in the shipped 1.48 build, and subscriptions are in-memory). A
trigger has no thread — its effect is materializing a Task. Signals are
adopted where they fit: the notifications/inbox phase. Design revision
recorded in docs/wip/agent-ops-target-architecture.md.

UI: the routines feature gains a trigger-type selector (schedule /
module event / inbound webhook), event name + JSON payload filter
fields, event chips in the list, and the webhook URL on the detail
page.

Live-validated: contacts_create → contacts.contact.created → task
materialized with payload + auto-dispatched; webhook fire with wrong
secret 401, right secret 200 + task with body attached.

commits.message:
Add notifications inbox on Mastra notifications storage

Task completions/failures and trigger errors now land in a durable team
inbox instead of only in task rows nobody watches.

Backend (apps/ai):
- src/notifications/inbox.ts — records created DIRECTLY on the Mastra
  notifications storage domain (ai.mastra_notifications), not via
  sendNotificationSignal (that is agent-to-agent delivery machinery:
  forces agentId, runs delivery policy, wakes threads). Records carry no
  deliverAt/summaryAt, so the built-in notification dispatcher never
  considers them due. Scoping rides a synthetic per-tenant inbox thread
  (inbox:{tenantId}) — the table has no tenant column and only filters
  on threadId/resourceId/agentId. The storage handle is imported lazily:
  the emitters sit inside the Mastra config's own dependency graph and
  an eager singleton import is a circular module-eval.
- Emitters: task-job finalize emits task_completed / task_failed (with
  result text payload and task metadata for deep links); the heartbeat
  onError hook emits trigger_failed, deduped per trigger while pending
  so a crashing schedule coalesces into one entry.
- /ai/v1/notifications routes: list, unseen-count, seen-all, per-id
  seen/dismiss — thin over the storage domain, tenant from the bearer.

Shell: admin-menu contributions accept a useBadgeCount hook, rendered by
an always-mounted per-item badge component on the app-bar icon rail
(first badge mechanism in the shell).

Tasks module UI: Posteingang/Inbox page (/mdl/tasks/inbox) with mark
seen/dismiss + mark-all, a sidebar item after Briefing with an unseen
count badge, an open-notifications section on the Briefing screen, and
the unseen badge on the tasks app-bar icon. Data layer (fetch + query
hooks) lives in ai-ui features/inbox, same split as routines.

Live-validated: webhook trigger -> task ENG-55 -> agent completed ->
task_completed record -> badges (app bar + sidebar), Briefing section,
inbox page; mark-all-seen persists and clears both badges.

commits.message:
fix(copilot): dock floating launcher & avatar to bottom-right on mode switch

The floating compact launcher was positioned from floatingPosition, whose
default was sized to the modal (FLOATING_DEFAULT_HEIGHT=148) while the launcher
renders at ~56px — so switching to floating dropped it mid-screen, and nothing
re-cornered either surface on mode changes.

- Size the launcher's bottom-right home to its own footprint via
  resolveLauncherCornerPosition (used for the initial position too).
- Re-dock both surfaces to the corner when switching to floating/mini-floating
  from the position menu (launcher via floatingPosition, avatar via clearing
  fabPosition/anchor).
- Add a floatingDockedToCorner flag + layout effect that keeps the resting
  launcher pinned as its measured height settles; cleared once the user drags.
- reanchorFloatingPositionToViewport keeps a corner-docked panel tracking its
  edges on window resize instead of only clamping.

Verified in-app: switch->floating, switch->avatar, and reload all land
bottom-right; window resize tracks the corner.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
Adopt Mastra memory quick wins: thread titles, working memory, history hygiene

Three memory adoptions on the chat substrate, verified against the
compiled @mastra/memory 1.21 / core 1.48 dist before wiring:

- Thread title generation: memory options.generateTitle synthesizes the
  title from the first exchange using the agent's own model (compiled
  fallback via getLLM when model is omitted); fires only while the
  thread is untitled. The two legacy title paths are DELETED so they
  cannot block the gate: the client-side first-message truncation
  (deriveInitialSessionTitleFromText / deriveInitialThreadTitleFromText,
  incl. the dead server-side maybeDeriveInitialSessionTitle orphan) —
  threads are now created untitled and lists fall back to summary/id
  until the title lands.

- Working memory (resource scope): a small bounded zod profile
  (language, role, focus, preferences, facts) injected each turn and
  maintained by the agent via the auto-registered updateWorkingMemory
  tool. The adapter's stub resource methods now persist for real by
  delegating to the pg memory domain (ai.mastra_resources), keyed
  `${tenantId}:${userId}` so profiles stay tenant-scoped while the
  Mastra resourceId remains the engenty user id. Settings view
  (Assistant memory) renders the profile read-only with a reset button,
  backed by GET/DELETE /ai/v1/memory/working.

- History hygiene on every assembled agent: ToolCallFilter strips bulky
  engenty_tool_execute transcripts from recalled history (the last two
  tool steps stay intact for the live loop) and TokenLimiterProcessor
  caps recalled history at 100k tokens.

Live-validated: German first message → synthesized German title
("Aktuelle zeitgesteuerte Routinen"); "merke dir…" turn → agent wrote
the schema profile to ai.mastra_resources; settings page renders it and
reset clears it.

commits.message:
Add Code Mode (read-only) on the copilot's Docker workspace sandbox

One `execute_typescript` tool: the model writes a single TypeScript
program that orchestrates tools as external_* functions in the run's
workspace sandbox — batching, filtering, and aggregation happen in code
instead of N chat round-trips.

- Tool set (v1): the discovery meta-tool (engenty_tools_search) plus a
  READ-ONLY execute variant (engenty_tool_execute_readonly). The
  read-only allow-list is enforced server-side in executeEngentyTool
  ({enforceReadOnly}) — non-read-only operations (risk above low, or
  approval-gated) are rejected with a clear pointer to the regular chat
  tool where the native approval gate applies. Typed per-operation
  stubs generated from contract JSON schemas are a later enhancement.

- DockerCodeModeTransport: the shipped StdioCodeModeTransport stages
  the program on the HOST and spawns node against a host path — which a
  Docker sandbox cannot see. This transport speaks the same wire
  protocol (frames on stdout, rpc-results on stdin; runner source from
  the exported buildRunner/buildProgramModule) but stages into the
  sandbox's bind-mounted working directory, lazily starts the
  container, and runs the program with bun (the unified sandbox image
  ships it). Host↔container path mapping is read from the pinned
  DockerSandbox instance fields — documented compiled-behavior
  coupling, re-verify per @mastra bump.

- Attach rule: root agents that carry the engenty catalog meta-tools
  AND run with a sandbox-carrying workspace; the code-mode usage
  contract + external_* stubs are appended to their instructions.

- The copilot workspace now enables the sandbox (session lifecycle,
  lazy container start — idle chats pay nothing). EXECUTE_COMMAND keeps
  its HITL approval gate; free-form CLI/code work stays delegated to
  the engenty.cli sub-agent.

Live-validated: one prompt → three iterating programs in the container
(a real TypeError propagated back through the RPC bridge, console.log
lines streamed as frames, then a program fetched all contacts via
external_engenty_tool_execute_readonly and aggregated in code) → one
correct result. Unit test covers the read-only guard both ways.

commits.message:
Replace the routine scheduler with Triggers backed by Mastra heartbeats

A Trigger is the single model for 'a reason work starts' (schedule |
event | manual) and always references a task template — firing a
trigger materializes a Task into the durable task pipeline. There are
no prompt-only routines.

- tasks module: module_tasks.triggers + task_templates (schema, DAL,
  gateway operations incl. triggers_fire as the one execution path
  shared by scheduled, manual, and future event fires).
- apps/ai src/scheduler/: Mastra heartbeats as the pure cron substrate.
  The prepare hook enforces quiet hours, fires the trigger via the
  service principal, and returns null so no agent ever runs; a no-op
  engenty.scheduler agent anchors the heartbeats (worker requirement).
  Reconcile syncs module ROUTINE.md declarations -> trigger rows ->
  heartbeats at boot (deferred: the module capability loader blocks
  during createApp) and on demand via POST /ai/v1/triggers/reconcile.
- /ai/v1/triggers routes replace /ai/v1/routines; system jobs
  (cleanup-interrupts) ride their own heartbeats; the pg_cron tick,
  due.ts cron parsing, ai.routine_state and ai.custom_routine are
  dropped (core migration). cron-parser dependency removed — Engenty
  parses no cron anymore.
- routines UI now speaks the trigger API: single schedule per routine,
  task-template payloads (name doubles as task title, instructions as
  task description).
- fix: the Session workspace fallback from the 1.48 migration threw at
  runtime ('Workspace requires at least a filesystem, sandbox, or
  skills') on runs without a workspace, e.g. headless task jobs — now a
  shared scratch-dir LocalFilesystem workspace that feeds no tools.

Validated live: trigger created via UI and API -> heartbeat row ->
minute-cron fire -> task materialized with correct template fields ->
dispatch consumer -> task-job workflow -> specialist run -> in_review;
enable/disable pause-resume, delete removes the heartbeat, boot
reconcile recreates system-job heartbeats.

commits.message:
Converge tool approvals onto native Mastra suspend/resume

Replace the abort-and-rerun decision-artifact approval flow with native
tool-level suspend/resume: engenty_tool_execute declares suspend/resume
schemas and suspends the run when a contract requires approval. The
Approve/Deny decision resumes the SAME parked run in place via
respondToToolSuspension — no re-run, no lost turn.

- approvalPolicy on the engenty-tools run context (suspend | deny |
  artifact; default deny, fail-safe): interactive chat suspends,
  delegated leaf runs deny (would deadlock the parent), voice keeps its
  artifact + /v1/realtime/tools/approve flow.
- Tool-approval interrupts persist as decision-kind open interrupts
  carrying the suspended run_id; the runs route routes them to the
  parked-session resume (not the artifact re-run branch), folds the
  Approve once/always grant into session metadata, and audits the
  decision. The write-back on interrupt-clear carries the just-persisted
  grant so it survives the resume.
- resumeConversationRun drives the continuation inside the engenty-tools
  ALS context so a second gated call in the continuation suspends again
  instead of being denied, with persisted grants threaded through.
- Full-page copilot chat: fall back to the persisted open interrupt when
  the transcript has no decision artifact to render (the suspended tool
  call has no result), matching the drawer.
- Restart recovery via listSuspendedRuns is deferred; parked sessions
  keep the frontend-tool 15-min TTL (documented in docs/wip).

  the transcript has no decision artifact to render (the suspended tool
  call has no result), matching the drawer.

  keep the frontend-tool 15-min TTL (documented in docs/wip).

commits.message:
Show the voice approval dialog in threadless voice sessions

A voice session started on a fresh chat has no active thread, and the
voice provider only parked a gated backend op's approval for the
confirmation dialog when a thread existed — without one, the raw
decision artifact went back to the voice model, which then narrated an
on-screen dialog that never rendered.

The dialog now always shows. With a thread, the decision persists as a
chat grant as before ('always' survives the whole chat). Without one,
the grant cannot be persisted, so the user's dialog decision rides the
re-invoke as a one-shot approval_grant_once on the execute call — the
same authority as the persisted-grant path (an explicit user decision on
the user's own bearer token), scoped to that single call.

commits.message:
Add event triggers: module-event bus + webhook ingestion onto triggers_fire

Phase 2 of the trigger cutover — event triggers fire the same
triggers_fire task materialization as schedule and manual triggers,
through two ingestion edges:

- provider_id 'module-events': the tasks plugin subscribes to the
  in-process plugin event bus (engenty.events.modules) for every
  canonical event name an enabled trigger listens to (exact-name
  subscriptions, replayed from the database on boot, extended on
  trigger create/update), applies the shallow event_filter payload
  match, and fires per matching tenant trigger.
- provider_id 'webhook': a public tasks-module route
  POST /api/tasks/trigger-hooks/:triggerId/:secret, authenticated by a
  per-trigger secret generated at creation (timing-safe compare, one
  generic 401 for every reject reason).

Both edges attach the event payload to the materialized task's
description so the agent works on the concrete occurrence. The fire
logic is extracted from the triggers_fire gateway op into a shared
fireTrigger (scoped to the trigger row's own tenant/scope), used by all
callers including the heartbeat hook path.

Mastra SignalProviders are deliberately NOT used: compiled-dist
verification showed they are thread-scoped (every subscription is a
(resourceId, threadId), delivery is sendNotificationSignal into a
thread, the documented POST /api/signals/:providerId route does not
exist in the shipped 1.48 build, and subscriptions are in-memory). A
trigger has no thread — its effect is materializing a Task. Signals are
adopted where they fit: the notifications/inbox phase. Design revision
recorded in docs/wip/agent-ops-target-architecture.md.

UI: the routines feature gains a trigger-type selector (schedule /
module event / inbound webhook), event name + JSON payload filter
fields, event chips in the list, and the webhook URL on the detail
page.

Live-validated: contacts_create → contacts.contact.created → task
materialized with payload + auto-dispatched; webhook fire with wrong
secret 401, right secret 200 + task with body attached.

commits.message:
Add notifications inbox on Mastra notifications storage

Task completions/failures and trigger errors now land in a durable team
inbox instead of only in task rows nobody watches.

Backend (apps/ai):
- src/notifications/inbox.ts — records created DIRECTLY on the Mastra
  notifications storage domain (ai.mastra_notifications), not via
  sendNotificationSignal (that is agent-to-agent delivery machinery:
  forces agentId, runs delivery policy, wakes threads). Records carry no
  deliverAt/summaryAt, so the built-in notification dispatcher never
  considers them due. Scoping rides a synthetic per-tenant inbox thread
  (inbox:{tenantId}) — the table has no tenant column and only filters
  on threadId/resourceId/agentId. The storage handle is imported lazily:
  the emitters sit inside the Mastra config's own dependency graph and
  an eager singleton import is a circular module-eval.
- Emitters: task-job finalize emits task_completed / task_failed (with
  result text payload and task metadata for deep links); the heartbeat
  onError hook emits trigger_failed, deduped per trigger while pending
  so a crashing schedule coalesces into one entry.
- /ai/v1/notifications routes: list, unseen-count, seen-all, per-id
  seen/dismiss — thin over the storage domain, tenant from the bearer.

Shell: admin-menu contributions accept a useBadgeCount hook, rendered by
an always-mounted per-item badge component on the app-bar icon rail
(first badge mechanism in the shell).

Tasks module UI: Posteingang/Inbox page (/mdl/tasks/inbox) with mark
seen/dismiss + mark-all, a sidebar item after Briefing with an unseen
count badge, an open-notifications section on the Briefing screen, and
the unseen badge on the tasks app-bar icon. Data layer (fetch + query
hooks) lives in ai-ui features/inbox, same split as routines.

Live-validated: webhook trigger -> task ENG-55 -> agent completed ->
task_completed record -> badges (app bar + sidebar), Briefing section,
inbox page; mark-all-seen persists and clears both badges.

commits.message:
Adopt Mastra memory quick wins: thread titles, working memory, history hygiene

Three memory adoptions on the chat substrate, verified against the
compiled @mastra/memory 1.21 / core 1.48 dist before wiring:

- Thread title generation: memory options.generateTitle synthesizes the
  title from the first exchange using the agent's own model (compiled
  fallback via getLLM when model is omitted); fires only while the
  thread is untitled. The two legacy title paths are DELETED so they
  cannot block the gate: the client-side first-message truncation
  (deriveInitialSessionTitleFromText / deriveInitialThreadTitleFromText,
  incl. the dead server-side maybeDeriveInitialSessionTitle orphan) —
  threads are now created untitled and lists fall back to summary/id
  until the title lands.

- Working memory (resource scope): a small bounded zod profile
  (language, role, focus, preferences, facts) injected each turn and
  maintained by the agent via the auto-registered updateWorkingMemory
  tool. The adapter's stub resource methods now persist for real by
  delegating to the pg memory domain (ai.mastra_resources), keyed
  `${tenantId}:${userId}` so profiles stay tenant-scoped while the
  Mastra resourceId remains the engenty user id. Settings view
  (Assistant memory) renders the profile read-only with a reset button,
  backed by GET/DELETE /ai/v1/memory/working.

- History hygiene on every assembled agent: ToolCallFilter strips bulky
  engenty_tool_execute transcripts from recalled history (the last two
  tool steps stay intact for the live loop) and TokenLimiterProcessor
  caps recalled history at 100k tokens.

Live-validated: German first message → synthesized German title
("Aktuelle zeitgesteuerte Routinen"); "merke dir…" turn → agent wrote
the schema profile to ai.mastra_resources; settings page renders it and
reset clears it.

commits.message:
Add Code Mode (read-only) on the copilot's Docker workspace sandbox

One `execute_typescript` tool: the model writes a single TypeScript
program that orchestrates tools as external_* functions in the run's
workspace sandbox — batching, filtering, and aggregation happen in code
instead of N chat round-trips.

- Tool set (v1): the discovery meta-tool (engenty_tools_search) plus a
  READ-ONLY execute variant (engenty_tool_execute_readonly). The
  read-only allow-list is enforced server-side in executeEngentyTool
  ({enforceReadOnly}) — non-read-only operations (risk above low, or
  approval-gated) are rejected with a clear pointer to the regular chat
  tool where the native approval gate applies. Typed per-operation
  stubs generated from contract JSON schemas are a later enhancement.

- DockerCodeModeTransport: the shipped StdioCodeModeTransport stages
  the program on the HOST and spawns node against a host path — which a
  Docker sandbox cannot see. This transport speaks the same wire
  protocol (frames on stdout, rpc-results on stdin; runner source from
  the exported buildRunner/buildProgramModule) but stages into the
  sandbox's bind-mounted working directory, lazily starts the
  container, and runs the program with bun (the unified sandbox image
  ships it). Host↔container path mapping is read from the pinned
  DockerSandbox instance fields — documented compiled-behavior
  coupling, re-verify per @mastra bump.

- Attach rule: root agents that carry the engenty catalog meta-tools
  AND run with a sandbox-carrying workspace; the code-mode usage
  contract + external_* stubs are appended to their instructions.

- The copilot workspace now enables the sandbox (session lifecycle,
  lazy container start — idle chats pay nothing). EXECUTE_COMMAND keeps
  its HITL approval gate; free-form CLI/code work stays delegated to
  the engenty.cli sub-agent.

Live-validated: one prompt → three iterating programs in the container
(a real TypeError propagated back through the RPC bridge, console.log
lines streamed as frames, then a program fetched all contacts via
external_engenty_tool_execute_readonly and aggregated in code) → one
correct result. Unit test covers the read-only guard both ways.

commits.message:
Retry scheduler service-scope resolution to survive the dev boot race

startScheduler() resolved the service principal's scope exactly once at
boot. When the AI app boots ahead of core in the turbo dev stack, the
core HTTP call fails (network_error, status 0), the scope resolves to
null, and the scheduler stays disabled for the whole process with only a
warning.

resolveSchedulerServiceScope() now distinguishes a missing
ENGENTY_AI_SERVICE_JWT (permanent — warn once, stay off) from a failed
resolution (core unreachable / JWT rejected — transient), and
startScheduler() retries the transient case on a bounded backoff
mirroring the existing reconcile deferral before giving up. The
resolution result is returned as a discriminated union so the two cases
log distinctly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
Add the external connections framework: central OAuth, per-action policies, connectors

One mechanism for external service connections, extensible via connector
modules, with a three-axis permission model enforced at the existing
operation gate (design: docs/wip/connections-framework.md).

- @engenty/connections-sdk: ConnectorDefinition/actions (read|write|
  destructive groups drive the static contract), globalThis-backed
  connector registry (per-plugin jiti module caches would otherwise
  split a module-level singleton), AES-256-GCM token crypto
  (CONNECTIONS_TOKEN_ENC_KEY), generic OAuth2 client, module_connections
  repo (withFreshAccessToken is the only token read path), allow/ask/
  deny policy resolution (action override > group override > default,
  with sharing and autonomous-mode clamps), and the runtime that
  projects connector actions into module operations.
- modules/connections: schema (connections, connection_action_policies,
  pending_oauth_flows, approval_requests; token columns excluded from
  the authenticated column grant), nonce-state OAuth connect/callback
  routes, management operations (catalog, settings, set_policy,
  disconnect, approvals list/decide, granted_operations), and the async
  profile policy: deny clamps are authoritative for every principal;
  user asks stay with the AI pre-gate; autonomous asks 202 and record a
  durable approval request. UI: settings + admin pages with the
  per-action allow/ask/deny matrix, sharing, autonomous mode, non-owner
  cap, pending-approvals table (en+de).
- Connectors: google (gmail/drive/calendar), microsoft (outlook mail+
  calendar, onedrive via Graph), slack (user-token, scopes via
  user_scope).
- Core: profile policies may be async (evaluatePolicy awaited at its
  three call sites).
- AI plane: chat/resume runs merge durable connection grants into the
  approval grants so 'always allow' skips the Approve card; new
  approvalPolicy 'defer' for headless task jobs passes gated calls
  through to core and shapes the 202 into an approval_pending result
  plus a tenant-inbox notification. Delegated in-chat leaf runs keep
  'deny'.

Follow-up (documented): automatic task re-dispatch on approval; MCP
connector kind.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
gmail stream: bound detail-fetch concurrency, back off on 429

The backfill fetched all page message details with one unbounded
Promise.all — Gmail's per-user concurrency cap answers 429
rateLimitExceeded ("Too many concurrent requests for user."). Fetch in
chunks of 5 and retry rate-limited requests with exponential backoff
(1s/2s/4s) before failing the pull.

early-return skipped op synthesis while the reload had already dropped

op until a full server restart (hit in the field: inbox_message_search
vanished after inbox UI edits, contacts survived because that module was
never reloaded). Unregister the stale entry and proceed; regression test.
